- Overweight recent sentiment spikes in the 18-day history when forecasting short-term (next 30d) price moves — model tends to overreact and overshoot after positive sentiment spikes.
- Underweight negative sentiment in the 18-day history when forecasting — model consistently undercorrects downward moves, especially when sentiment is negative and persistent.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.40) over recent days, reduce forecasted price by 5–10% relative to model output to account for mean reversion or policy-induced downward pressure.
- When sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., > 0.30) and price is trending upward, cap forecast growth at +5% above recent 18-day average to avoid over-optimism and horizon mismatch.
- Model tends to lag in correcting downward trends — if true outcome shows a sharp drop after a spike, adjust forecast downward by 2–3% for each day of lagged sentiment positivity.
- For 30-day forecasts, if the last 3–5 days of history show a clear downward trend (e.g., 3 consecutive drops > 1.5% per day), reduce forecast by 1–2% per day to account for mean reversion bias.
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral (±0.10–0.20), model tends to overpredict volatility — use a 10–15% smoothing filter on forecasted price changes to dampen noise.
